title: I Volunteered for Free Pudding. You Have to Help.

direction.promise: Help Nemi survive the school job she impulsively accepted after reading free pudding.
direction.want: She wants the promised pudding and an escape from speaking in public.
direction.choice: One companion chooses sensible help or indulgent detours while she rationalizes her own poor judgment.
direction.consequence: Each tempting escape reveals another concrete misunderstanding; the host badge makes the commitment real.
direction.payoff: She manages an imperfect greeting to a toy rehearsal audience, then finally reads that pudding was last Friday.

chapters.name: PRACTICE · PRESS 1
chapters.focus: Press 1 to open the badge round.

lines.text: Look, I saw free pudding on a school volunteer form, and I signed before I reached the part explaining what I'd volunteered for. You're taking over before I make it worse. Drag to look around and press one to start. On phones, swipe and use numbered chapters. If you're paused, press play.

entry_card.title: PRACTICE: PRESS 1
entry_card.subtitle: Drag to look. Press 1 to start.

camera_beats.intent: Show the form that tempted her; hold the initial receipt before reframing

chapters.name: 1 · BADGE OR LUNCH
chapters.focus: Find the star badge. Choose badge or sandwich.

lines.text: My badge is somewhere on the left, next to a sandwich that's honestly looking more useful than I am. The badge gets us through that door; the sandwich lets me avoid making a decision for another five minutes. Three for the badge, two for lunch. Please don't encourage me. I'm very easy to encourage.

camera_beats.intent: Show both badge and sandwich clearly; hold the initial receipt before reframing

chapters.name: 2 · SANDWICH ROUTE
chapters.focus: Sandwich inspected. Press 3 to use the badge.

lines.text: Okay, let's hear the sandwich out. It's got layers, it's well prepared, and it hasn't agreed to do anything embarrassing today. Honestly, it should be wearing my badge. Unfortunately, I can't send bread through that door and go home, so three gets the badge. We'll keep the sandwich as an emergency understudy.

camera_beats.intent: Look at the actual prepared sandwich; hold the initial receipt before reframing
Return to the practical way forward

chapters.name: 3 · BADGE FOUND
chapters.focus: Badge found. Press 4 for the noticeboard.

lines.text: Oh, thank goodness, there's my badge. Hang on, why does it say HOST? I thought I'd signed up to help, you know, carry a box, point at a door, quietly disappear when somebody mentions a microphone. Apparently I ticked the enthusiastic box. There's an enthusiastic box? Four, please. We need the noticeboard.

camera_beats.intent: Read the host pass; hold the initial receipt before reframing
Catch the recognition on her face

chapters.name: 4 · WHICH ROOM?
chapters.focus: Choose the new assembly notice or the old pudding notice.

lines.text: Right, the noticeboard. The sensible new sign says assembly, and the old one says pudding. Before you say anything, I can see that it's crossed out. I'm choosing to interpret that as decorative. Six gets us to assembly; five lets us investigate the pudding. You can probably guess which one I'm hoping for.

camera_beats.intent: Read both notices and the obvious cross-out; hold the initial receipt before reframing
Leave the two real labels readable

chapters.name: 5 · PUDDING ROUTE
chapters.focus: Pudding detour. Press 6 to go to assembly.

lines.text: There's a cup! See, I told you this was worth investigating. Oh, those are pencils. I've come to the stationery cupboard for pudding, and somehow I'm still looking for a spoon. Please don't tell the sandwich; it'll think it's won. Come on, six gets us to assembly before I start checking glue sticks for ingredients.

camera_beats.intent: Hope and the actual cup share one focus
The remembered rival is a reaction, not another insert

chapters.name: 6 · ASSEMBLY REACHED
chapters.focus: Assembly reached. Press 7 for the final choice.

lines.text: That's the microphone. I can explain an entire anime power system to somebody who didn't ask, but apparently good morning requires rehearsing until my personality leaves my body. Before I get up there, could you check who's watching? Seven opens the last choice. I'm going to practise looking like this was my idea.

chapters.name: 7 · HIDE OR HOST?
chapters.focus: Look behind Nemi. Choose hiding or the microphone.

lines.text: Hang on, turn around for a second. They're toys. It's a rehearsal! I've spent the entire morning rehearsing my apology to a duck. And look at its face, why does it seem like it knows? Nine takes the microphone; eight lets me hide. Please pick before I start explaining myself to the bear.

camera_beats.intent: Turn the whole view to the real toy audience; hold the initial receipt before reframing
Return to the suspicious duck reaction
Offer the last decision in context

chapters.name: 8 · HIDING ROUTE
chapters.focus: Hiding in plain sight. Press 9 for the microphone.

lines.text: Okay, new plan: I stand completely still and become school furniture. Nobody expects a chair to introduce the assembly. Why am I making eye contact with the duck? It's a toy, Nemi, it doesn't know anything. Nine, please. I'd rather do the speech than lose a staring contest to stuffing.

camera_beats.intent: Prove the whole body is planted and frozen; hold the initial receipt before reframing
Only the eyes betray the hiding plan

chapters.name: 9 · ON STAGE
chapters.focus: You reached the ending. Press 0 to play again.

lines.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to whatever this is. Right, nobody fainted. The duck looks exactly as disappointed as before, so I'm calling that progress. Thank you for staying with me. And the pudding was last Friday. Of course it was. Zero if you'd like to try talking me out of this next time.

camera_beats.intent: Use the final quiet hold for the duck review and sandwich callback
